title: Working at Redwood — Roles, Career Ladders, Benefits, Hiring & Onboarding, and Internal Tools
author: Ava Martinez
body:
Overview

Purpose
This document is the canonical company handbook chapter for Engineers, Product, and cross-functional teammates joining Redwood. It summarizes how we work, role definitions and career ladders, primary benefits and perks, the hiring and onboarding flow, and a practical internal tools guide for day‑one productivity. Maintain this page via the People Ops handbook repo and submit changes as PRs to the handbook team.

Audience
All Redwood employees and hiring managers. Use this as the single source of truth for role expectations, compensation framework references (high level), and onboarding checklists.

Sections
1) Working at Redwood — ways of working and culture
2) Roles & career ladders — expectations by function and level
3) Benefits & perks — summary and eligibility
4) Hiring & onboarding — process, timelines, and checklists
5) Internal tools guide — accounts, access, sample commands
6) FAQs and escalation

---

1) Working at Redwood — ways of working and culture

Intro
Redwood is an engineering-first, product-oriented company focused on reliable, cost-efficient LLM inference. We value clarity, ownership, and operational rigor. Below are our core working principles and common practices.

Core principles
- Ship small, measure often: short feedback loops with evals and telemetry included in every rollout.
- Shared ownership: teams own the full lifecycle of the features they ship (design, infra, SLOs, rollout).
- Observability-first: every new service or route must include dashboards, alerts, and error budgets.
- Blameless postmortems: focus on fixes and improvement, not fault assignment.

Meetings & communication
- Default async: use Slack for low-latency coordination, Confluence for documented decisions.
- Weekly team syncs: 30–45 minutes max; preserve heads‑down time.
- Quarterly roadmap reviews and company all‑hands.

Work location & time policies
- Hybrid-first with flexible remote policies; teams agree on core overlap hours where applicable.
- Redwood provides a remote-office stipend and a home-office setup budget (see Benefits).

---

2) Roles & career ladders

Overview
We maintain function-specific career ladders for Engineering, Applied ML, Product, SRE, and Design. Each ladder describes responsibilities, impact expectations, managerial scope (if applicable), and sample success criteria. Below are condensed summaries; full role profiles live in the Careers Playbook.

Engineering ladder (individual contributor focus)
- E1 / Associate Engineer: Learning the codebase, shipping small fixes, participating in pair-programming.
- E2 / Software Engineer: Owns features, writes tests and docs, contributes to system design.
- E3 / Senior Software Engineer: Designs components, mentors others, leads medium projects end-to-end.
- E4 / Staff Engineer: Cross-team design, drives technical strategy, visible system ownership.
- E5 / Principal Engineer: Defines long-term architecture, major cross-domain initiatives, technical mentorship at scale.

Product ladder (PM)
- PM1: Executes on scoped features, writes requirements, coordinates with Eng and DX.
- PM2: Defines roadmaps for a product area, owns metrics and experiments.
- PM3 / Senior PM: Drives multi-quarter strategy, commercial outcomes, and cross-functional alignment.

Applied ML ladder
- AML1: Implements evals and model onboarding basics.
- AML2: Designs evaluation harnesses, quantization experiments.
- AML3: Owns model quality programs and degrades strategies for production.

Manager and leadership expectations
- First-line managers balance people ops (1:1s, career growth) and deliverables.
- Promotion to manager requires demonstrated coaching ability, hiring impact, and delivery leadership.

Promotion process (high level)
1. Candidate prepares a written case with examples mapped to the ladder criteria.
2. Manager gathers feedback from peers and cross-functional partners.
3. Panel review with 3–5 reviewers from the function.
4. Final decision documented and next-step plan created.

---

3) Benefits & perks (summary)

Eligibility
Most full-time employees are eligible for primary benefits after the standard waiting period (30–60 days). Contractors have a subset of benefits; check your contract.

Health & financial benefits
- Medical, dental, and vision plans (multiple plan tiers; company covers a portion of premiums).
- 401(k) with company match (up to 4% of salary).
- Equity grants by role level (initial grant + refresh cycles for long-tenured employees).

Time off & leave
- Generous paid time off (flexible PTO policy) and company-wide holidays.
- Parental leave: primary caregiver 18 weeks; secondary caregiver 8 weeks (paid).
- Sabbatical eligibility after 5 years.

Work-from-home & office
- Remote stipend: USD 1,000 (one-time) for home-office setup.
- Monthly coworking allowance available for those using third-party spaces.

Learning & development
- Annual learning stipend: USD 2,000 for conferences, courses, books.
- Internal mentorship program and biweekly technical brown-bags.

Other perks
- Commuter benefits; pre-tax options where available.
- Wellness allowance and mental health EAP access.
- Company equipment: standard laptop (M-series MacBook Pro / equivalent), additional monitors on request.

Benefits contacts
- People Ops benefits lead: Priya Shah (people-ops-benefits@redwood.example).
- Payroll & 401k: payroll@redwood.example.

---

4) Hiring & onboarding overview

Hiring stages (standard process)
1. Requisition & hiring rubric: hiring manager writes role summary and success metrics.
2. Sourcing & screening: recruiter screens candidates for basics and culture fit.
3. Technical interviews: 2–3 loop with coding, system design, and role-specific interviews.
4. Onsite / virtual onsite: cross-functional interviews including manager and potential peers.
5. Offer & negotiation: compensation band check, approval from People Ops.
6. Background check and reference checks.
7. Acceptance & preboarding.

Average timelines
- Candidate to offer: 3–6 weeks for typical roles.
- Preboarding duration: 1–4 weeks depending on notice period and role.

Preboarding checklist (for hiring manager)
- Create org chart and 30/60/90 goals for hire.
- Request equipment via IT (standard laptop + monitor).
- Add new hire to team Slack channels and calendar invites for orientation.
- Assign buddy and onboarding mentor.
- Provision necessary accounts (see Internal tools).

First 30 days — recommended onboarding plan
Week 0 (before start): set up accounts, send welcome packet, team intro.
Week 1: orientation (Company all-hands, People Ops welcome), security training, simple first task with pairing.
Weeks 2–4: deeper onboarding with product walkthroughs, shadowing, and a first small deliverable.

Manager responsibilities for onboarding
- Weekly 1:1 and clear goal-setting at day 3.
- Weekly check-ins with buddy and engineering mentor.
- Early feedback checkpoints at 2 and 6 weeks.

Exit & offboarding summary
- Submit termination in HRIS, revoke access following the offboarding runbook, schedule knowledge transfer, and collect equipment. See Offboarding Runbook in eng-developer-experience.

---

5) Internal tools guide — accounts, access, and sample commands

Account & access flow
- Identity provider: Redwood uses SSO with Okta. New hires receive an Okta invite during preboarding.
- Access tiers: new hire (day 1 restricted), contributor (project-level), admin (requires approval).
- Request additional access via the Access Request form (People Ops portal) or by filing a ticket in the IT Jira project: INFRA-ACCESS.

Primary tools and owners
- Slack (communications) — owner: Eng DX team
- Confluence (docs) — owner: People Ops / Eng DX
- GitHub (code) — owner: Eng Platform
- Jira (task tracking) — owner: Eng Platform and Product Ops
- Redwood Console (internal dashboards) — owner: Eng Platform
- redwoodctl (CLI) — owner: Eng Serving Runtime
- Datadog / Honeycomb (observability) — owner: Eng SRE

Sample redwoodctl usage
- Authenticate: redwoodctl login --sso
- Lists active routes for a team: redwoodctl routes list --team infra
- Tail logs for a service: redwoodctl logs tail --service model-proxy --since 1h
- Trigger a canary rollout: redwoodctl rollout start --service inference-api --strategy canary --percent 10

Account setup quick steps (day 0/1)
1. Accept Okta invite and set MFA (recommended: hardware key + authenticator app).
2. Sign in to GitHub and accept organization invite.
3. Join core Slack channels: #eng, #product, #people-ops, #announcements, #help-desk.
4. Complete mandatory security and compliance training in Confluence > Security & Compliance.

Secrets & credential guidance
- Use the company secrets manager (vault.redwood.example) for all production credentials. Do not store secrets in code or public repositories.
- For local development, request a scoped service token with a 30-day expiry and rotate monthly.

---

6) FAQs and escalation

Q: Who do I contact about payroll discrepancies?
A: Payroll team at payroll@redwood.example and cc your manager.

Q: How do I request additional headcount?
A: Submit a hiring request through the People Ops hiring form and attach a one-page justification and metrics.

Escalation path for urgent people items
1. Immediate manager
2. People Ops lead (Priya Shah)
3. Head of People Ops
4. CEO (for legal/regulatory escalations)
